The package installs into standard system paths (`/usr/lib`, `/usr/bin`, `/opt/ghidra`) and sets appropriate permissions. Dependencies and conflicts are declared correctly. The <.SRCINFO> file is metadata used by the Arch User Repository (AUR) to describe the package and its sources. It lists two main sources: a specs tarball and a Ghidra plugin ZIP, both hosted on the official GitHub repository of the project (Noelo-Lab/kuna). The binary artifacts are prebuilt and distributed via GitHub Releases, which is a common practice for Rust-based tools when targeting multiple architectures (x86_64 and aarch64). The checksums (sha256sums) are provided for all sources, including architecture-specific binaries, ensuring integrity verification.

The sources are fetched over HTTPS from GitHub, a trusted and expected origin for this package. There are no signs of obfuscated URLs, suspicious redirects, or external domains. The package does not execute arbitrary scripts during build or install, nor does it pull code at runtime. The use of prebuilt binaries is typical for AUR packages ending in "-bin", and the checksums match the expected standard for such packages. While the binaries are not built from source in this package, that is a packaging choice, not a security violation.

The dependencies and conflicts are appropriate: glibc and libgcc for runtime support, and optional dependency on ghidra-extension-kuna-bin for integration. No dangerous commands, network calls, or file operations are present in this metadata file, as it is not executable. The file adheres to standard AUR packaging practices and shows no evidence of malicious intent or supply-chain compromise.
</details>
